tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. An answer item with empty selected and no custom means the user skipped that question: continue without it, do not ask it again, and do not treat the skip as permission.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: excel_create
tools.description: Create a new .xlsx Excel workbook in the session workspace from structured sheets. Each sheet has a name and an array of rows; each row is an array of scalar cells (string, number, boolean, or null). Use excel_update to change an existing workbook without recreating it.

path.description: Output path. Relative paths resolve against the session workspace; the extension must be .xlsx.

sheets.description: Sheets to write, in tab order.

rows.description: Grid rows; the first row is typically a header row. String cells starting with = are written as formulas.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when it already exists. Defaults to false.

tools.name: excel_read
tools.description: Read one or all sheets of an existing .xlsx workbook and return each sheet as rows of scalar values (formatted strings). Formula cells return their cached value when one exists; formulas without a cached value return the formula as an "=SUM(…)" string. Rows are capped; the per-sheet `truncated` flag reports when more rows were not returned. Pass `sheet` to read a single named sheet.

path.description: Path to the .xlsx file, relative to the session workspace or absolute inside it.

sheet.description: Read only this worksheet by exact name. Omit to read every sheet.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows returned per sheet. Defaults to 5000.

tools.name: excel_update
tools.description: Update an existing .xlsx workbook in place: replace or create whole sheets by name (`sheets`) and/or write individual scalar values into cells (`cell_updates`, e.g. "B2"). The workbook is re-published as an ASCII-safe package, so binary-only extensions cannot survive; prefer excel_create for new workbooks. Provide at least one sheet or cell update.

path.description: Path to the existing .xlsx file.

name.description: Worksheet to replace; created when absent.

cell.description: Cell address in A1 notation, e.g. "B2".

value.description: Scalar value to write into the cell. A string starting with = is written as a formula.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: list_subagent_models
tools.description: Inspect subagent models without changing the current Agent. No arguments: providers; `provider`: allowed models; `provider` + `model`: that model and its reasoning efforts. Inspect options here before selecting a child provider and model; use returned ids for delegation.

tools.name: load_workspace_dependencies
tools.description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

tools.name: modlens_read_image
tools.description: Read an image through the modlens vision bridge. Use whenever a message references an image the current model cannot see: a local file path or an http(s) URL to a screenshot, photo, chart, diagram, or document scan. Returns structured evidence with every word transcribed (ocr.full_text), layout regions in reading order, semantics, and an uncertainty list. Quote the evidence instead of guessing. For the same image and focus, call this tool once and reuse its returned evidence instead of calling again. Evidence for a pasted image carries an `attachment-id:` line: to read that image again with a new focus, pass the id as path, and do not search the filesystem for the file. Requires a configured modlens engine (run `npx @liustack/modlens doctor` in a terminal to check).

path.description: Absolute local file path, http(s) URL, or the attachment-id (sha256:...) from pasted-image evidence

prompt.description: Optional extra focus for the reading (e.g. "focus on the axis labels")

tools.name: pdf_extract_latex
tools.description: Extract a PDF with formulas turned into LaTeX. Use this INSTEAD of pdf_extract_text whenever the pages contain math (textbooks, lecture slides, papers): the text layer stores formulas as loose glyphs, so pdf_extract_text loses subscripts/Greek/operators. Modes: 'ocr' whole-page OCR (best for slide decks, scans, WPS/PowerPoint exports), 'hybrid' keeps the pdfjs text layer and only replaces rows whose text layer is already garbled with $$LaTeX$$ (best for arXiv/LaTeX/Word papers), 'auto' picks by PDF producer and per page falls back to OCR when a page's text layer is mostly broken. Returns Markdown with $...$ / $$...$$. First call loads local models and is slow (tens of seconds); after that expect 5-20 s per page on CPU.

path.description: Absolute path of the local PDF file.

pages.description: Pages to process, e.g. "3", "1-3,5", "all". Default: first 3 pages.

mode.description: auto (default) = choose by PDF producer; ocr = whole-page OCR; hybrid = text layer + formula replacement.

scale.description: Render scale for the OCR input, default 2.5 (≈180 DPI).

maxPages.description: Cap when pages is omitted, default 3.

tools.name: pdf_extract_text
tools.description: Extract text from a local PDF. By default returns one entry per page with the page text; withPosition also returns per-line coordinates (y/x in PDF units, y up from the page bottom). Engine auto-selects: pdfjs first, falling back to a built-in decoder for PDFs whose CJK text pdfjs cannot map. Triggers: PDF text, read PDF, extract PDF content, parse PDF.

path.description: Absolute path of the local PDF file.

page.description: Optional 1-based page number; default: all pages.

withPosition.description: Also return per-line x/y coordinates and font size.

engine.description: Force an extraction engine; default auto (pdfjs first, built-in decoder as fallback).

tools.name: pdf_info
tools.description: Read PDF metadata: page count, page sizes, document info, and the font list with an embedded flag for each font. Triggers: PDF info, inspect PDF, check PDF fonts, page count.

path.description: Absolute path of the local PDF file.

tools.name: pdf_render_page
tools.description: Render one page of a local PDF to a PNG file and return its local path. Engine auto-selects: pdfjs first, falling back to a built-in system-font renderer when pdfjs errors or produces a blank page (for PDFs with non-embedded CJK fonts, e.g. EasyEDA exports). Triggers: render PDF page, PDF to image, view PDF page.

path.description: Absolute path of the local PDF file.

scale.description: Render scale relative to the PDF page size, default 2.

engine.description: Force a render engine; default auto.

tools.name: plugin_manager
tools.description: List plugins or bundles in the current profile, enable or disable them, install a bundle, or remove an installed bundle. Every action requires danger-full-access permission or approval for this call. Approval does not change the session permission mode. Changes affect every session in this profile. List first to obtain exact identifiers. Package installation can execute allowed build scripts. Live profiles apply changes immediately, including upgrades of installed packages; a change result that is not applied carries nextStep, which says what to do or tell the user. Unmet DSH version requirements (engines.dsh, else DSH peer dependencies) block installation and activation. Version exemptions risk crashes and data loss: warn the user and obtain explicit permission for the exact plugin and runtime versions before granting one.

target.description: Plugin entry id, bundle package name, or installation spec, according to action. For an Official catalog entry, pass list_bundles installTarget.spec to install_bundle.

enabled.description: Required for set operations; defaults to true for installation. For set_version_exemption, true grants and false revokes.

runtimeVersion.description: For set_version_exemption: exact DSH version from list_version_exemptions. Target must be the manifest package-name@version, not an alias or version range.

acceptRisk.description: For granting an exemption: true only after warning the user about possible crashes and data loss and receiving explicit permission for this exact plugin/runtime pair. General installation permission is not enough.

approvedBuilds.description: For install_bundle: pass names from pendingBuilds only after the user explicitly approves running their install scripts in the conversation. This grants persistent permission for this profile.

registry.description: For install_bundle: the npm registry URL asked first, when the user names one; otherwise the configured registry is asked, and its configured fallbacks while a registry is unreachable.

limit.description: List page size, from 1 to 100; defaults to 25.

tools.name: ppt_create
tools.description: Create a PowerPoint .pptx presentation in the session workspace (16:9 widescreen, 13.33 x 7.5 in). Optionally start with a title slide, then add slides with a title, body paragraphs, bullet points, speaker notes, and linked PNG/JPG/GIF images. Images are linked, not embedded: give x/y/w/h in inches for explicit placement (sizing: contain fits inside the box, cover fills it and crops), or omit them for automatic placement below the text at natural size. The result echoes every element's landing position (inches) and a text wireframe sketch of each slide, so you can verify the composition you authored.

path.description: Output path. Relative paths resolve against the session workspace; the extension must be .pptx.

title.description: Deck title. When provided, a title slide is inserted before the explicit slides.

slides.description: Slides in presentation order. Optional when a title is provided.

paragraphs.description: Body paragraphs rendered as plain text boxes.

bullets.description: Bullet list items rendered after the paragraphs.

images.description: Images linked on this slide, drawn after the text content.

path.description: Image file inside the session workspace: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, or .gif. The deck links to it, so keep the file in place.

x.description: Left position in inches on the 13.33x7.5 slide. Omit for automatic placement below the text.

y.description: Top position in inches. Omit for automatic placement.

w.description: Display width in inches. Omit to use the intrinsic size (PNG/JPG/GIF headers are sniffed).

h.description: Display height in inches. Omit to use the intrinsic size; a single dimension scales by aspect.

sizing.description: Fit mode inside the w x h box: contain fits whole (default), cover fills and crops. Requires w and h.

alt.description: Alt text; defaults to the image path.

overwrite.description: Replace the file when it already exists. Defaults to false.

tools.name: ppt_read
tools.description: Extract the content and layout of an existing .pptx presentation. Per slide, in slide order: paragraphs, tables (rows of cell texts), speaker notes, linked/embedded image count, image alt texts — plus an `elements` array giving every shape's bounding box in inches (x/y/w/h) and the deck canvas size, with a text wireframe sketch of each slide. Table cell text is reported under `tables`, not duplicated into `paragraphs`. Use it to understand, summarize, or re-layout a deck: the element boxes tell you exactly where everything sits on the canvas.

path.description: Path to the .pptx file, relative to the session workspace or absolute inside it.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters returned across the deck. Defaults to 200000.

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Hosts may show presented files only after your turn ends, so call it once the files are final. If the user needs to review files earlier, such as before a tool call that waits for their answer, link them in your message instead. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence as scheduledAt in UTC and scheduledAtLocal in the zone of rrule. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes.

rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

target.description: this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory and preset. With this_session or new_once, a delivery waits until the previous one finishes, and only the latest occurrence that passed meanwhile is delivered. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

content.text:
The user wants me to start the sample app (demo-app) and the test platform so they can manually test.

Context: 62 days have passed since the last session (now 2026-11-25). The environment may have changed (DSH upgraded, session logs v4). The platform code was last modified 2026-09-21, though AGENTS.md mentions more work.

Task: start demo-app (port 4517) and platform (port 4519), and give the user the URLs. Also per AGENTS.md: archive at turn start, check the watcher.

Important: starting long-running servers via background jobs. Earlier, starting the platform server in the sandbox worked for API, but Web cases needed chromium (escalation only for browser). For the user's manual testing, they'll click "运行" in the UI — which may include Web cases → the platform server needs to spawn Chromium → in my sandbox it gets EPERM. That's a real problem: if I start the server via a sandboxed background job, Web UI cases will fail with "Chromium 启动失败: spawn EPERM".

So I should start the platform server with wider permissions (danger-full-access) so that Web cases work when the user runs them manually. That requires an approval prompt — acceptable and justified.

Also the demo app doesn't need browser, but starting both in one escalated command is simpler. Alternatively start the demo app normally and the platform escalated.

Plan:
1. Archive at turn start (--quiet) + check watcher log (per AGENTS.md).
2. Check ports 4517/4519 are free; check data dir state (db.json may contain stuff).
3. Check that dependencies/browsers/dist still exist (62 days later, files should still be there; but let me verify web/dist and node_modules exist).
4. Start demo-app on 4517 (escalated? it doesn't need spawn — normal is fine).
5. Start platform on 4519 WITH escalation (so Chromium works for Web cases).
6. Wait, then verify both respond: GET demo health, GET platform health, and confirm frontend is served.
7. Tell the user the URLs and a quick test script (what to click), including: 导入示例 → 选择标签/运行 → 看日志 → 报告. Also credentials for the shop (admin/123456).
8. Archive at end.

Note the GUI URL in the runtime context is http://127.0.0.1:3080 — that's the DSH GUI, not our platform. The platform will be at http://127.0.0.1:4519.

Let me also consider: should I open the browser for the user? `Start-Process` from sandboxed pwsh may be denied (spawn). With the escalated platform start, I could also open the browser in the same escalated command. But maybe the user prefers to open it themselves. I'll try to open it in the escalated command (nice touch) — actually opening a browser window from a server process command is fine. But it might be surprising. The user said "帮我启动...我手动测一下" → they'll interact. Opening the browser is helpful. Let me do it in one escalated command: start both servers via a single command? They're two long-running processes; I need background jobs.

Approach: use `node tools/demo.mjs --serve` — it starts both servers (spawn children) AND opens the browser, then keeps running. That's exactly the "demo environment" mode I built. It needs spawn → escalation. One command, one escalation, both servers + browser.

Risk: demo.mjs spawns children with `stdio: 'inherit'`; in the escalated pwsh job that should work. It also opens the browser via `cmd /c start` (spawns cmd — allowed in full access).

But: if the job dies (e.g., when my turn ends?), the servers die. Background jobs are managed by the DSH process; they continue after the turn. Previously, background jobs persisted until finished/killed. But now the GUI is the *desktop* profile possibly, and the session has been resumed 62 days later — the old jobs are gone.

Given this, `demo.mjs --serve` as a background job is reasonable. Alternatively start each server separately as two background jobs (more granular control, and the platform server one escalated). demo.mjs --serve also imports example automatically? No: --serve just starts servers and opens the UI (no auto-run). Good.

However, demo.mjs --serve prints "按 Ctrl+C 结束" and waits — perfect.

But there's a subtlety: demo.mjs binds PLATFORM_PORT 4519 and DEMO_PORT 4517 by default. Good.

One concern: does `node tools/demo.mjs --serve` in the escalated job open a browser on the user's desktop? `cmd /c start <url>` should. Nice.

Another concern: the platform's data/db.json currently may be empty (I reset it on 09-21) or contain stuff from later sessions (files may have changed in the 62 days — AGENTS.md mentions other work happened). The user will import the example anyway. Let me check db.json quickly.

Also: 62 days later, is `code/node_modules` still present? Should be, unless deleted. Let me verify key paths: code/node_modules/playwright, code/.playwright-browsers/chromium-*, code/web/dist/index.html.

Let me do the checks first (archive + paths + ports), then start.

Note: the AGENTS.md says the current DSH uses session log v4 and `pickSessionLog()` takes the max version — the archive script was updated accordingly. Good; my archive run should work.

If my click happened before the examples list loaded (modal shows "正在读取示例清单…"), `.example-item button` wouldn't exist yet → firstVisible would wait up to 8s. It found something (no error) — maybe it found a *different* button? `.example-list button` doesn't exist before load.

Hmm, but there's one thing: the recording instance's data dir was fresh (empty db). The home page shows the empty state with 「导入示例」 button in the sidebar. Then the modal never opens. Then the editor step skipped, then the run button missing → error.

That's very likely: the empty state says: `点「导入示例」一键体验，或「新建」创建第一个项目。` → `text=导入示例` matches that paragraph. But the first selector `button:has-text("导入示例")` should match the sidebar button first (it's in the list before the text selector). `firstVisible` iterates selectors in order: first `button:has-text("导入示例")` — if visible, returns it. The sidebar button should be visible...

Unless the sidebar's 导入示例 button is `button.btn` with text "导入示例" — yes (ProjectBar line ~350). So it should match.

Hmm. But then `importBtn.click()` opens the modal. Then `firstVisible(['.example-item button', '.example-list button'])` → the modal's import button. Click → import.

Wait — maybe the click on `.example-item button` hit a *disabled* button? `disabled={importingId !== null}` — initially null, so enabled.

```js
  })).catch(() => null)
  log(`[UI@${label}]`, JSON.stringify(info))
}
```

Wait: sequence: after report scroll (~33s), I set caption 09 and goto DEMO. The frame at 33s shows the report with caption 09 — because `caption()` on the report page happened before the goto? Let me re-read my code order:

```js
// 场景 8
await caption(page, '这就是被测软件...', '09 被测软件')
await page.goto(`${DEMO}/`, ...)
```
The caption is injected on the *report page*, then we navigate away → caption disappears (new page). So during the transition, the report had the 09 caption momentarily. That's the f33 frame. Then on the shop page there's NO caption (since navigation wiped it) until... after the shop interactions I set caption 10. So during the shop login/checkout, there's no caption (just "09 被测软件" for a few hundred ms on the report).

Also: after going back to the platform (场景 9), I set caption 11 before goto → same issue: caption injected on shop page then wiped.

So captions for navigation steps are lost. Fix: set the caption AFTER navigation (and optionally use addInitScript to persist captions across navigations).

Better approach: install an init script that re-creates the caption bar on every page load with the latest text stored in a global (sessionStorage). Then:
```js
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  const text = sessionStorage.getItem('__rec_cap_text') || ''
  const sub = sessionStorage.getItem('__rec_cap_sub') || ''
  ... create bar on DOMContentLoaded
})
```
and `caption()` writes to sessionStorage AND updates the DOM. That way each navigation restores the caption.

That's a clean fix. Let me implement:

```js
async function caption(page, text, sub = '') {
  await page.evaluate(({text, sub}) => {
    try { sessionStorage.setItem('__rec_cap_text', text); sessionStorage.setItem('__rec_cap_sub', sub) } catch {}
    ... original DOM injection ...
  }, {text, sub})
}
```
And add the init script right after creating the page:
```js
await page.addInitScript(() => {
  const render = () => {
    let text = '', sub = ''
    try { text = sessionStorage.getItem('__rec_cap_text') || ''; sub = sessionStorage.getItem('__rec_cap_sub') || '' } catch {}
    if (!text) return
    let bar = document.getElementById('__rec_caption')
    if (!bar) { create...; document.documentElement.appendChild(bar) }
    bar.innerHTML = ...
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', render)
  else render()
})
```
This restores the last caption on every navigation — good for continuity.

Also the frame at f33 shows the report page — meaning the 09 caption appeared while the report was displayed (stale). With the fix, when I set caption 09 BEFORE goto, the report briefly shows 09... still the same issue in the instant before navigation. Better: reorder to set the caption AFTER each goto. - For the report step: goto report → caption 08 → scroll.

- For the back step: goto platform → caption 11 → click 执行记录.

### 讲解词（可直接照读）

> 这是一个通用的软件测试平台。它支持两类测试：HTTP 接口测试，和基于 Playwright 的 Web 界面测试。
> 所有用例都是声明式的：请求怎么发、变量怎么串、断言怎么写，都在界面里配置，不需要写代码。
> 现在我用它来测一个示例的小商城——这个商城我故意留了 4 个缺陷，看看平台能不能发现它们。
> 点全部运行……可以看到每个用例、每个步骤都在实时输出日志；断言逐条给出通过或失败。
> 11 个用例：7 个通过，4 个失败。报告里写得很清楚：期望运费 10 元，实际 0 元；期望折扣按商品小计计算，
> 实际把小计加运费一起算了；库存不足也没拦住；Web 用例那边，结算金额只显示了整数部分。
> 失败时平台自动截了图，这就是证据。
> 另外，已知缺陷的用例可以标记成「预期失败」，这样 CI 就不会因为已知问题一直红着；
> 反过来如果它意外通过了，平台会提醒你缺陷可能已经修好。
> 最后，平台自身也有自测脚本，退出码为 0 才说明平台是完好的——可以放进 CI。

![封面](video/20261125-小商城示例-全流程测试-封面.jpg)

## 我是怎么"自己操作 + 自己录"的

不是模拟点击的假动画，而是**真浏览器驱动真界面**：

- 用 Playwright 启动 Chromium，`recordVideo` 直接录制浏览器画面（不是截屏拼帧）；
- 脚本按 11 个场景真实点击（导入示例 → 打开用例 → 运行全部 → 看断言 → 开报告 → 被测软件 → 执行记录），**每步底部有字幕**、点击前目标元素会高亮红框；
- 录完用带 x264 的 ffmpeg 转成 mp4，并自动生成录像说明、报告附件和封面帧。

执行结果（视频里真实出现，不是旁白）：**11 个用例 · 7 通过 / 4 失败 / 0 异常**，4 条失败正好是示例小商城植入的缺陷：

| 用例 | 视频里的失败断言 |
| --- | --- |
| 小额订单应收取运费 | 期望等于 10，实际 0 |
| 优惠券应按商品小计计算折扣 | 期望等于 5.99，实际 6.99 |
| 库存不足应拒绝下单 | 期望等于 400，实际 200 |
| 结算合计金额显示正确（Web） | 期望匹配 `/\d+\.\d{2}/`，实际「合计：52 元」 |

## 关键设计（为什么可以放心重复录）

| 点 | 做法 |
| --- | --- |
| **不污染你的数据** | 录制用独立实例：端口 `4521` + 数据目录 `code/.recording-data`；你正在用的 `4519` 完全没动（刚复查：4517/4519 都还健康） |

## 上传内容

- `readme.md`、`AGENTS.md`、`.gitignore`
- `code/`：`server/src`（7 个后端模块）、`web/src`（React 界面 12 个文件）、`examples/demo-app`（示例被测软件 + 11 个用例 + 缺陷说明）、`tools/`（14 个工具：演示/自测/验收/录屏/归档等）、`docs/平台实现与测试方法.md`、构建配置
- `video/`：`20261125-小商城示例-全流程测试.mp4`（50.8 秒）+ 说明、报告、封面
- `prompt/`：4 个会话的对话正文 / 会话全文 / 原始事件（含子代理会话）
- `.dsh/`：hook 与 profile 补丁配置

**按 `.gitignore` 排除**（未上传）：`node_modules/`、`.npm-cache/`、`.playwright-browsers/`、`code/data/`（运行时数据与截图）、`code/web/dist/`（构建产物）、`.recording-*`。

## 过程中的两处障碍与处理

1. **TLS 报错** `schannel: SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS` → 改用 OpenSSL 后端（已写入本仓库配置 `http.sslBackend=openssl`）。
2. **拿不到凭据**：仓库里有 `credential.helper=wincred` 但被沙箱禁止创建命名管道（`sh.exe couldn't create signal pipe`）→ 在放宽权限后，用你 Windows 凭据管理器里已保存的账号（`sssyi2`）完成推送。**你的密码/令牌我没有看到，也没有写到任何文件里。**

## 以后怎么更新

在你自己的终端（不受沙箱限制）里：

```powershell
cd E:\testPlatform
git add -A
git commit -m "说明本次改动"
git push
```

凭据管理器已存好，正常不需要再输入密码。**如果让我来推送**，每次会弹一次权限确认（沙箱限制所致），这是预期行为。

## 两个可选建议

- 仓库现在没有 `LICENSE`，如果需要开源协议我可以补一个（例如 MIT），并写进 readme。
- GitHub 上的仓库还没填 Description 和 Topics（如 `testing`、`playwright`、`test-automation`）；这属于网页设置，需要你在仓库页面里填，或者给我一个有 `repo` 权限的令牌我用 API 设置。
